01 — project

SmartMenu

A full-stack React app that recommends Indian dishes by mood and wellness goals, filtered against dietary preferences, allergies, and weather.

Category

Full-stack · recommendation engine

Stack

React · Vite · localStorage auth

My role

Solo rebuild

The problem

"What should I eat?" is a genuinely hard question when you factor in mood, health goals, dietary restrictions, allergies, and even the weather outside — and most food apps only solve for cuisine type or cravings, not the fuller picture. The original version of this project was AI-generated and broke down under real use, so it needed a proper rebuild.

The approach

I rebuilt SmartMenu from scratch on React with Vite, treating it as a real application rather than a prototype. At the core is a filtering engine that layers several inputs at once: a regional Indian cuisine dataset, mood-based recommendation logic, wellness goals, dietary preferences and allergies, and current weather — narrowing a full cuisine dataset down to a handful of dishes that actually fit the moment.

Authentication runs on localStorage rather than a backend user system, keeping the app lightweight while still letting each user's preferences persist across sessions. The interface uses a warm cream-and-brown design system, paired with Playfair Display and Inter, to make the food itself feel like the visual focus rather than generic app chrome.

What it does

  • Recommends dishes based on mood and wellness goals, not just cuisine type
  • Filters against dietary preferences and allergies automatically
  • Factors current weather into what it suggests
  • Persists user preferences locally without needing a backend account system

Why it matters

This project is as much a lesson in rebuilding on solid foundations as it is a recommendation engine — taking something that looked complete on the surface but didn't hold up, and re-architecting it properly rather than patching around the cracks.
